rationale: The pain is real but narrow: open-source maintainers with AI-content policies who encounter Copilot bot activity on their repos. This population is a mix of unpaid volunteers and enterprise GitHub admins — the former won't pay for a governance tool, and the latter are likely to wait for GitHub's own platform controls. Willingness to pay is weak (score 3) and buyer clarity is poor (score 4) because the paying sub-segment is hard to isolate. Total of 4.1 falls below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: Not recommended for pursuit. The addressable paying audience — enterprise GitHub admins with an explicit AI-content policy AND budget for a third-party enforcement tool — is too small and too hard to reach to justify building. GitHub itself is the natural platform to solve this, and any third-party solution is likely to be deprecated when GitHub ships native controls.
notes: Fails willingness_to_pay_min (3 < 5) and buyer_clarity_min (4 < 6) build gates. Total (4.1) is below validate threshold (5.5) — drop.
